Classical and Bayesian Evaluation of Experimental Matrices

design-efficiency-1.1.Rd

Evaluate response-surface experimental matrices using classical information criteria, region-specific prediction variance, prior-informed posterior covariance, simulation-based assurance, explicit cost summaries, and sequential augmentation.

bayes_design_efficiency(design, reference = NULL,
  model = c("second_order", "first_order", "pseudoquadratic"),
  powers = 0.5, region = NULL, grid_n = 7L,
  style = c("standard", "briones2002"))

bayes_compare_designs(designs, reference = NULL, ...)

bayes_design_region_sensitivity(design, regions,
  criterion = c("I", "G", "trace", "A", "D"),
  model = c("second_order", "first_order", "pseudoquadratic"),
  powers = 0.5, grid_n = 7L)

bayes_design_rank(designs,
  model = c("second_order", "first_order", "pseudoquadratic"),
  powers = 0.5, region = NULL, grid_n = 7L)

bayes_design_cost_efficiency(design,
  criterion = c("A", "D", "I", "G"), cost_per_run = 1,
  fixed_cost = 0, reference = NULL, ...)

bayes_design_information(design,
  model = c("second_order", "first_order", "pseudoquadratic"),
  powers = 0.5, region = NULL, prior_sd = 2.5, sigma = 1,
  grid_n = 7L)

bayes_rsm_assurance(design,
  model = c("second_order", "first_order", "pseudoquadratic"),
  powers = 0.5, region = NULL, prior_sd = 2.5, sigma = 1,
  n_sim = 200L,
  target = c("precision", "curvature", "interior_optimum"),
  precision_threshold = 0.5, curvature_threshold = 0.1,
  curvature_probability = 0.95, interior_probability = 0.80,
  posterior_draws = 200L, seed = 20260826)

bayes_rsm_augment(design, n_add = 1L,
  criterion = c("D", "A", "I", "G", "BayesI"),
  candidate_levels = c(-1.5, -1, 0, 1, 1.5), candidates = NULL,
  model = c("second_order", "first_order", "pseudoquadratic"),
  powers = 0.5, region = NULL, prior_sd = 2.5, sigma = 1,
  seed = 20260826)

Arguments

design

Candidate response-surface design.

reference

Optional reference design for relative comparisons.

model

Model basis assumed when evaluating information.

powers

Pseudoquadratic transformation powers.

region

Prediction region.

grid_n

Integration-grid resolution.

style

Standard relative criteria or the run-adjusted convention used in the 2002 Agrociencia comparison.

designs

Named list of candidate designs.

...

Additional arguments passed to design-efficiency calculations.

regions

Named list of alternative prediction regions.

criterion

Information or augmentation criterion.

cost_per_run

Positive marginal cost per experimental run.

fixed_cost

Non-negative fixed experimental cost.

prior_sd

Prior standard deviation for model coefficients.

sigma

Planning residual standard deviation.

n_sim

Number of simulated future experiments.

target

Assurance target.

precision_threshold

Maximum posterior coefficient SD used by the precision target.

curvature_threshold

Minimum absolute canonical eigenvalue considered practically curved.

curvature_probability

Posterior probability required for the curvature target.

interior_probability

Posterior probability required for the stationary point to lie inside the region.

posterior_draws

Posterior coefficient draws per simulated experiment.

seed

Random seed.

n_add

Number of runs added during augmentation.

candidate_levels

Candidate grid levels.

candidates

Optional explicit candidate points.

Value

Data frames or planning objects containing design criteria, criterion-specific ranks, relative efficiencies, posterior-covariance criteria, assurance probabilities, or an augmented bayes_rsm_design.

Details

A/D criteria reward parameter information, whereas I/G criteria focus on prediction. These criteria can disagree, so the package reports them separately instead of declaring a universal winner. For style="briones2002", relative A, I, G and covariance-determinant criteria use the reference-to-candidate precision ratio with the source article's run-count adjustment. Bayesian planning criteria additionally condition on declared coefficient priors and residual noise assumptions.

References

Briones-Encinia, F. and Martínez-Garza, A. (2002). Eficiencia de algunos diseños experimentales en la estimación de una superficie de respuesta. Agrociencia, 36(2), 201–210.

Examples

ccd <- bayes_ccd(c("x1", "x2"))
f3 <- expand.grid(x1 = c(-1,0,1), x2 = c(-1,0,1))
bayes_design_efficiency(ccd, f3, style = "briones2002")
#>   n_runs rank n_terms        A        D         I     G  trace determinant
#> 1     13    6       6 6.075949 7.397245 0.2895062 0.625 0.9875      163840
#>   covariance_determinant condition_number_scaled relative_A relative_D
#> 1           6.103516e-06                1.140175   1.499513   21.88034
#>   relative_I relative_G
#> 1   1.210431  0.8923077
bayes_design_information(ccd, prior_sd = 2)
#>   n_runs n_terms posterior_trace posterior_logdet bayesian_A bayesian_D
#> 1     13       6       0.9367973        -12.24705     6.4048   7.699654
#>   bayesian_I bayesian_G
#> 1  0.2778378  0.6008393
bayes_rsm_augment(ccd, n_add = 1, criterion = "I")
#> <bayes_rsm_design>
#>   Type: augmented_ccd_circumscribed
#>   Runs: 14
#>   Factors: coded_x1, coded_x2
